findings.detail: In the multi-variant branch `stats.startingPrices++` fires once per variant row, while in the single-variant branch it fires once per service. `WebScraperTab.tsx:198` renders the two counters in one sentence — `${s.services} services in ${s.categories} categories, ${s.startingPrices} with a starting price` — which reads as a subset of the service count. A venue with 3 services that each expose 2 "from" variants logs "3 services in 1 categories, 6 with a starting price". No user data is wrong, only the log; the test venue has `withOptions: 0` so this never triggers on the captured fixture, which is why the suite doesn't catch it. It would be medium if the number were exported rather than logged.
findings.summary: startingPrices counts option rows, not services, so the log line can exceed the service count

findings.detail: `handbooks/architecture/frontend-boundaries.md` § "What Rex flags" lists `fetch(` appearing in a file under `components/`, and `(u, init) => fetch(u, init)` matches that pattern literally. Recording it as a deliberate non-violation rather than silently skipping it: the component calls a service (`fetchFreshaVenue`), all URL construction, headers, status handling and the abort timer live in `services/freshaVenueService.ts`, and the arrow function only hands the service the browser primitive via the `FetchTextLike` port. That is what makes the module testable without a network — `tests/unit/freshaVenue.test.ts:180-202` exercises success, 451, missing data and timeout with no DOM. It is also the pattern already established at `WebScraperTab.tsx:63` for `fetchYallaMenu`, so this diff follows the file's convention rather than introducing a new one. No action required.
findings.summary: Literal `fetch(` in a component is an injected transport, not component-owned I/O
